Senses.Explanation: The idiom of secondhand realization — riding the empty, catching echoes — the masters' charge against heirs who take the hollow of the ancestors' words and pass on only the sound, from the Song halls to the Qing. Mi'an Xianjie, at the Wuju mountain hall, sweeps the whole apparatus away — wedge driven out by wedge turns into ruts, mind transmitted by mind deepens the sickness, Bodhidharma missed the head-on word and faced the wall nine years — and the descendants after him ride the empty and catch echoes: raised brows and blinking eyes, staff-work and shout-work, all leaves stopping a baby's cry, while Wuju goes straight up with no road to heaven and no door into earth, teeth clenched, kneading mud and water with them until the staff falls: without one bout of bone-piercing cold, how could the plum blossom scent the nose; Dahui Zonggao, eulogizing two Chan men at their stupa, walks the seal down the line — Baiyun sold it cheap to the board-carrying man, Wuzu pasted it over with three pounds of hemp, Yuanwu his teacher scattered all three hundred sixty bones and eighty-four thousand pores into the assembly's laps — then draws a border with the staff that may not be crossed, and breaks the seal before them all so the descendants each get a livelihood of their own, spared riding the empty and catching echoes and dulling one another down the line; eyelashes and brows all fallen and the onlookers laugh without end; Zhongfeng Mingben works Xiangyan's enlightenment verse line by line — one strike and all knowing forgotten, the nod and the ancient road, no trace anywhere, dignity beyond sound and sight — then rules the men everywhere who claim the Way: which of them truly says the uppermost vehicle? They ride the empty and catch echoes; hence what covers heaven and earth must flow out of your own chest, and next to it the seers-and-hearers school-solutions count ten against a hundred; Tianyin Yuanxiu raises Shitou and Yaoshan — words and deeds no concern, not-words and not-deeds no concern either, a needle will not enter here, flowers planted on stone — grants the two elders the stringless zither and its birthless song, father and son squared; yet the family shame shows to bystanders, and the man who rides the empty and catches echoes had best not touch it: touch it, thirty blows. Yinyuan Longqi spends the idiom on the carriers themselves — the great clamor Bodhidharma carried east to this soil; riding the empty and catching echoes, the Sixth Patriarch hauled it over the Lingnan ranges; they thought the ferrying of beings done, and how many monks are still unwilling — so Huangbo breaks the clods where it stands, levels the high and fills the low, lifts when it lifts, releases when it releases; Tian'an Sheng, run through the maze of delusion and awakening at the Qingzhou hall — how many trip on flat ground, watching the moon above and losing the oar in hand — and when the monk, three bows in, answers much-obliged for the master's instruction, gets back two words: a man riding the empty and catching echoes; then the said-or-not-said turned once more — to speak is surplus, not to speak is dulling; if spoken, what has been spoken; if not, what are the teeth chattering now; Yulin Tongxiu takes up Xuefeng as rice-cook under Deshan — bell not yet rung, drum not yet beaten, where does the old man carry his bowl? — big Deshan never got the last word, and next day, the master risen different from usual, Yantou claps and laughs: glad the old man has it, none under heaven can touch him, and even so only three years to live — and Yulin rules the echo-catcher glosses over Deshan while the strength-or-weakness bender buries Yantou: the mountain monk reports it straight to the schools, teacher strong and heir strong, give it back to the Deshan father and son; and Yunwai Xingze holds up the Diamond Sutra at the Qizhou Bodhi hall — one raw-iron spine of a World-Honored One standing ten thousand fathoms, barely knocked by Subhuti and rolling off into the grass — yet a man who enters the water knows the tall one: had the sutra stopped at thus-abide and thus-subdue, where would today's echo-riding men grope for it? The mountain monk is otherwise — hearing willing indeed, World-Honored One, joyful to hear — pierced straight through.
